items.informal_name: Commutativity of Variable Renaming and Expansion in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : ℕ) (f : σ → τ) (φ : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((MvPolynomial.expand p) φ) = (MvPolynomial.expand p) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ)
items.informal_description: For any type $\sigma$, commutative semiring $R$, and polynomial $\varphi \in R[\sigma]$, renaming variables followed by expansion is equivalent to expansion followed by renaming. Specifically, for any variable substitution function $f : \sigma \to \tau$ and integer $p$, we have $\text{rename}_f(\text{expand}_p(\varphi)) = \text{expand}_p(\text{rename}_f(\varphi))$, where $\text{expand}_p$ raises each variable to the $p$-th power and $\text{rename}_f$ applies the substitution $f$ to variable indices.

items.informal_name: Commutativity of Renaming and Expansion in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : ℕ) (f : σ → τ),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f).comp (MvPolynomial.expand p) = (MvPolynomial.expand p).comp (MvPolynomial.rename f)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \tau $, function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, and exponent $ p $, the composition of the variable renaming homomorphism $ \text{rename}_f : R[\sigma] \to R[\tau] $ with the expansion homomorphism $ \text{expand}_p : R[\sigma] \to R[\sigma] $ commutes. That is, $ \text{rename}_f \circ \text{expand}_p = \text{expand}_p \circ \text{rename}_f $ as $ R $-algebra homomorphisms, where $ \text{expand}_p $ raises each variable to the $ p $-th power and $ \text{rename}_f $ substitutes variables according to $ f $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Series Expansion at r is R-Linear
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring S] (p : Polynomial R) (r : R) (f : R →+* S),
  Polynomial.map f ((Polynomial.taylor r) p) = (Polynomial.taylor (f r)) (Polynomial.map f p)
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a semiring $ R $, the Taylor series expansion at $ r $ is an $ R $-linear map from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself, which sends each polynomial $ f $ to the polynomial obtained by substituting $ X + r $ into $ f $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (r : R), ↑↑(Polynomial.taylorEquiv r) = Polynomial.taylor r
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, the Taylor isomorphism is an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $. The coercion of this isomorphism to a function coincides with the Taylor series expansion map sending $ f $ to $ f(X + r) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Variable Renaming with Univariate Polynomial Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} {τ : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (a : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f).comp (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial a) = Polynomial.toMvPolynomial (f a)
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $ and any $ a \in \sigma $, the composition of the multivariate polynomial variable renaming homomorphism induced by $ f $ and the univariate polynomial embedding at $ a $ equals the univariate polynomial embedding at $ f(a) $. Formally, $ \text{rename}_f \circ \text{toMvPolynomial}_a = \text{toMvPolynomial}_{f(a)} $ as $ R $-algebra homomorphisms.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Variable Renaming with Univariate Polynomial Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} {τ : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (a : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((Polynomial.toMvPolynomial a) p) = (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial (f a)) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, element $ a \in \sigma $, and polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, renaming variables in the multivariate polynomial obtained by substituting $ X $ with $ a $ in $ p $ according to $ f $ yields the same result as substituting $ X $ with $ f(a) $ in $ p $ and then converting to a multivariate polynomial. Formally, $ \text{rename}(f)(p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(a)) = p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(f(a)) $.

items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (k : σ → τ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R)
  (g : τ → MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename k) (MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (g ∘ k) p) =

items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over $ R[\sigma] $, renaming the variables according to $ k $ after evaluating with the constant polynomial map $ C $ and variable map $ g \circ k $ is equivalent to evaluating the renamed polynomial with the constant polynomial map $ C $ and the renamed variable map $ \text{rename}_k \circ g $.

items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R) (j : τ)
  (g : σ → MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename (Prod.mk j)) (MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C g p) =
    MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (fun x => (MvPolynomial.rename (Prod.mk j)) (g x)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \tau $, polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, and variable mapping $ g : \sigma \to R[\tau] $, renaming the evaluation of $ p $ with coefficients via the constant polynomial embedding $ C $ and variables via $ g $ using the product map $ \prod.mk j $ is equivalent to evaluating $ p $ after renaming each variable in $ g $ with $ \prod.mk j $. Formally, $ \text{rename}(\prod.mk j, p.\text{eval}_2(C, g)) = p.\text{eval}_2(C, \lambda x. \text{rename}(\prod.mk j, g(x))) $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Aeval and Rename Equals Aeval of Composed Map
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  (k : σ → τ) (g : τ → S) [inst_2 : Algebra R S],
  (MvPolynomial.aeval g).comp (MvPolynomial.rename k) = MvPolynomial.aeval (g ∘ k)
items.informal_description: For any algebra $ S $ over a commutative semiring $ R $, the composition of the evaluation homomorphism $ \text{aeval}(g) $ with the renaming homomorphism $ \text{rename}(k) $ equals the evaluation homomorphism $ \text{aeval}(g \circ k) $. In symbols: $ (\text{aeval}(g)) \circ (\text{rename}(k)) = \text{aeval}(g \circ k) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Evaluation with Variable Renaming in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  (k : σ → τ) (g : τ → S) (p : MvPolynomial σ R) [inst_2 : Algebra R S],
  (MvPolynomial.aeval g) ((MvPolynomial.rename k) p) = (MvPolynomial.aeval (g ∘ k)) p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ in the ring $ R[\sigma] $, variable renaming function $ k : \sigma \to \tau $, and algebra homomorphism $ g : R[\tau] \to S $, the evaluation of the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(k, p) $ via $ g $ equals the evaluation of $ p $ via the composed homomorphism $ g \circ k $. Formally, $ \text{aeval}(g)(\text{rename}(k, p)) = \text{aeval}(g \circ k)(p) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Composition with Algebra Evaluation Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  (f : σ → S₁) {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (φ : S₁ →ₐ[R] B),
  φ.comp (MvPolynomial.aeval f) = MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => φ (f i)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $B$ equipped with an $R$-algebra structure and any algebra homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to B$ over $R$, the composition of $\phi$ with the multivariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism $\text{aeval}_f$ equals the evaluation homomorphism $\text{aeval}_{\phi \circ f}$, where $f : \sigma \to S_1$ is a variable assignment. This expresses that applying $\phi$ after polynomial evaluation is equivalent to first composing $\phi$ with the variable assignment and then evaluating.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Renamed Multivariate Polynomial Equals Direct Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → MvPolynomial τ R)
  (p : MvPolynomial σ R), (MvPolynomial.aeval id) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = (MvPolynomial.aeval f) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to R[\tau] $ and polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, the evaluation of the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(f, p) $ using the identity map on $ \tau $ is equal to the evaluation of $ p $ using the function $ f $. This establishes that substituting variables via renaming and then evaluating with the identity is equivalent to directly evaluating with the substitution function $ f $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Evaluation Homomorphism with Variable Renaming
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  (f : R →+* S) (k : σ → τ) (g : τ → S) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom f g) ((MvPolynomial.rename k) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom f (g ∘ k)) p
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S_1 $, variable assignment $ g : \sigma \to S_1 $, and renaming function $ k : \tau \to \sigma $, evaluating the renamed polynomial $ \mathrm{rename}\,k\,p $ using $ f $ on coefficients and $ g $ on variables is equivalent to evaluating the original polynomial $ p $ using $ f $ on coefficients and the composed assignment $ g \circ k $ on variables. Formally, $ \mathrm{eval}_2(f, g)(\mathrm{rename}\,k\,p) = \mathrm{eval}_2(f, g \circ k)(p) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Renaming and Evaluation in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} {S : Type u_5} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  (f : R →+* S) (k : σ → τ) (g : τ → S) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.eval₂ f g ((MvPolynomial.rename k) p) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ f (g ∘ k) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \tau $, multivariate polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, renaming function $ k : \sigma \to \tau $, coefficient map $ f : R \to S_1 $, and variable map $ g : \tau \to S_1 $, the evaluation of the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(k, p) $ with coefficient map $ f $ and variable map $ g $ is equal to the evaluation of $ p $ with coefficient map $ f $ and variable map $ g \circ k $.
